sections.html: Tometes makue was described only in 2002. It may reach a total length of about 40 cm. It is a hardy fish and as undemanding as one is used to from Myleus.
It is reported from Brasil (Rio Negro basin) and Venezuela (Caroni basin and Orinoco basin).
Compared with the "broadbands" (Myleus schomburgkii), the new import was quarrelsome, but not much information on the behaviour of such a rare new importation can be given yet.

The species has been mis-identified several times: by Kner in 1860 as Mylesinus schomburgkii, followed by Nelson (1961), Hurtado Sepulveda (1989), Lasso et al. (1995), and Machado-Allison & Fink (1995). Other mis-identifications are as Myleus setiger and Utiaritichthys sennaebragai, then followed the original description as Tometes makue.

Jégu, M. , G. M. dos Santos & E. Belmont-Jégu (2002): Tometes makue n. sp. (Characidae: Serrasalminae), une nouvelle espèce du bouclier guyanais décrite des bassins du Rio Negro (Brésil) et de l’Orénoque (Venezuela). Cybium v. 26 (no. 4): 253-274.
